sections.heading: String Functions
sections.body: C also has many useful string functions, which can be used to perform certain operations on strings. To use them, you must include the <string.h> header file in your program:

sections.heading: String Length
sections.body: For example, to get the length of a string, you can use the strlen() function:

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: In the Strings chapter, we used sizeof to get the size of a string/array. Note that sizeof and strlen behaves differently, as sizeof also includes the \0 character when counting:

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: It is also important that you know that sizeof will always return the memory size (in bytes), and not the actual string length:
sections.code:
char alphabet[] = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ";
printf("%zu\n", 
  strlen(alphabet));   // 26
printf("%zu\n", 
  sizeof(alphabet));   // 27

sections.heading: Example
sections.code:
char alphabet[50] = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ";
printf("%zu\n", 
  strlen(alphabet));   // 26
printf("%zu\n", sizeof(alphabet));   // 
  50
